    def t_shift(
    self,
    *,
    groupby: str | None = None,
    adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    spec: LBShiftSpec | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Baseline → worst post-baseline shift table per parameter (LBT03).

    A true cross-tabulation: per parameter, each subject contributes
    one ``"<BNRIND> to <ANRIND>"`` shift cell, where ANRIND is their
    worst post-baseline range indicator (NORMAL < LOW < HIGH <
    LOW LOW < HIGH HIGH — deterministic clinical rank, HIGH breaking
    the LOW/HIGH tie).  Baseline records are excluded (``ONTRTFL``
    preferred, else null-safe ``ABLFL``); subjects without a
    baseline indicator are excluded.

    Percentages are intentionally not emitted: the correct
    denominator is subjects with both a baseline and a post-baseline
    result per parameter, which needs per-cell denominator support
    in the engine (next round) — a percentage against the arm big-N
    would be wrong.

    Args:
        groupby: Treatment-arm column.
        adsl: ADSL DataFrame for the arm universe and big-N rows.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: {cards}-compatible ARD (subject counts).

    Examples:
        ``ard = adlb.tlg.lb.t_shift(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)``
    """
    spec = spec or LBShiftSpec()
    group_col = groupby or (spec.columns[0] if spec.columns else "TRTA")
    spec.validate_dataframe(self._df, group_col=group_col)
    post = self._df.filter(pl.col("ANRIND").is_not_null())
    if "ONTRTFL" in post.columns:
        post = post.filter(pl.col("ONTRTFL") == "Y")
    elif "ABLFL" in post.columns:
        post = post.filter(pl.col("ABLFL").ne_missing("Y"))
    worst = worst_case(
        post,
        by=["USUBJID", group_col, "PARAMCD"],
        order_col="ANRIND",
        order=spec.anrind_order,
    )
    shift = worst.filter(pl.col("BNRIND").is_not_null()).with_columns(
        (pl.col("BNRIND").cast(pl.Utf8) + " to " + pl.col("ANRIND").cast(pl.Utf8)).alias(
            "SHIFT"
        )
    )
    return summarize_ard(
        shift,
        rows=["PARAMCD", "SHIFT"],
        stats=spec.statistics,
        context="t_lb_shift",
        group_col=group_col,
        pools=spec.pools,
        column_order=spec.column_order,
        adsl=adsl,
        adsl_filter=spec.adsl_filter,
        dataset_filter=spec.dataset_filter,
        nested=True,
    )

    def t_abnormal(
    self,
    *,
    groupby: str | None = None,
    adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    spec: LBAbnormalSpec | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Laboratory abnormalities not present at baseline (LBT04).

    Per parameter and direction (Low = LOW / LOW LOW, High = HIGH /
    HIGH HIGH), following ``crane::ard_tabulate_abnormal``:

    - denominator ``N`` = subjects with ≥1 post-baseline assessment
      whose baseline is **not** abnormal in that direction;
    - numerator ``n`` = those with any post-baseline value in the
      direction;
    - ``pct`` = n / N (null when N = 0 — never fabricated).

    Post-baseline means ``ONTRTFL == "Y"`` when present, else
    non-baseline via null-safe ``ABLFL``.  Without a ``BNRIND``
    column no baseline exclusion is applied.

    Args:
        groupby: Treatment-arm column.
        adsl: ADSL DataFrame for the arm universe and big-N rows.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: {cards}-compatible ARD.

    Examples:
        ``ard = adlb.tlg.lb.t_abnormal(group_col="TRTA", adsl=adsl)``
    """
    spec = spec or LBAbnormalSpec()
    group_col = groupby or (spec.columns[0] if spec.columns else "TRTA")
    spec.validate_dataframe(self._df, group_col=group_col)
    if spec.pools or spec.header_rows:
        raise SchemaError(
            "t_abnormal does not support pools or header_rows yet — "
            "its per-cell denominators need dedicated engine support."
        )
    source = self._df
    if group_col not in source.columns:
        raise SchemaError(
            f"Group column '{group_col}' not found in the analysis dataset. "
            f"Available: {sorted(source.columns)}"
        )
    dataset_filter = resolve_filter(spec.dataset_filter)
    if dataset_filter is not None:
        source = source.filter(dataset_filter)
    post = source.filter(pl.col("ANRIND").is_not_null())
    if "ONTRTFL" in post.columns:
        post = post.filter(pl.col("ONTRTFL") == "Y")
    elif "ABLFL" in post.columns:
        post = post.filter(pl.col("ABLFL").ne_missing("Y"))
    post = post.with_columns(pl.col("ANRIND").str.to_uppercase().alias("__anrind"))

    context = "t_lb_abnormal"
    if adsl is not None:
        if group_col not in adsl.columns:
            raise SchemaError(f"Group column '{group_col}' not found in adsl.")
        big_n = compute_big_n(adsl, group_col, [], filter_expr=resolve_filter(spec.adsl_filter))
        data_arms = set(post[group_col].drop_nulls().unique().to_list())
        unknown = sorted(data_arms - set(big_n))
        if unknown:
            raise SchemaError(
                f"Arm(s) {unknown} in the analysis dataset have no denominator in ADSL."
            )
        arms = sorted(big_n)
    else:
        big_n = {}
        arms = sorted(post[group_col].drop_nulls().unique().to_list())
    if spec.column_order:
        arms = [a for a in spec.column_order if a in arms] + [
            a for a in arms if a not in spec.column_order
        ]

    rows_out: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    if adsl is not None:
        rows_out += [
            ard_row(group_col, arm, "", "", "N", "N", big_n.get(arm), context) for arm in arms
        ]

    directions = {"Low": spec.low_values, "High": spec.high_values}
    has_baseline = "BNRIND" in source.columns
    baseline = (
        source.with_columns(pl.col("BNRIND").str.to_uppercase().alias("__bnrind"))
        if has_baseline
        else None
    )
    for param in sorted(post["PARAMCD"].drop_nulls().unique().to_list()):
        p_post = post.filter(pl.col("PARAMCD") == param)
        for direction, levels in directions.items():
            base_abnormal: set[str] = set()
            if baseline is not None:
                base_abnormal = set(
                    baseline.filter(
                        (pl.col("PARAMCD") == param) & pl.col("__bnrind").is_in(levels)
                    )["USUBJID"].to_list()
                )
            for arm in arms:
                a_post = p_post.filter(pl.col(group_col) == arm)
                eligible = set(a_post["USUBJID"].to_list()) - base_abnormal
                abnormal = set(
                    a_post.filter(pl.col("__anrind").is_in(levels))["USUBJID"].to_list()
                )
                n = len(abnormal & eligible)
                denom = len(eligible)
                pct = round(n / denom * 100, 1) if denom > 0 else None
                lineage = {"group2": "PARAMCD", "group2_level": str(param)}
                rows_out += [
                    ard_row(
                        group_col, arm, "ABNORMAL", direction, "n", "n", n, context, **lineage
                    ),
                    ard_row(
                        group_col,
                        arm,
                        "ABNORMAL",
                        direction,
                        "N",
                        "N assessed",
                        denom,
                        context,
                        **lineage,
                    ),
                    ard_row(
                        group_col,
                        arm,
                        "ABNORMAL",
                        direction,
                        "pct",
                        "n / N (%)",
                        pct,
                        context,
                        **lineage,
                    ),
                ]

    ard = rows_to_ard(rows_out)
    issues = validate_ard(ard)
    if issues:
        raise SchemaError("ARD output failed schema validation:\n  " + "\n  ".join(issues))
    return ard

    def l_listing(
    self,
    *,
    spec: LBListingSpec | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Produce a laboratory abnormalities listing DataFrame.

    Selects rows with a non-normal range indicator (``ANRIND``) and
    returns the requested columns, sorted per spec.

    Args:
        spec: Optional ``LBListingSpec`` override.  If ``None``, the
            default spec is used.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: A plain DataFrame with the requested columns,
            sorted per spec.

    Examples:
        Default lab listing::

            listing = adlb.tlg.lb.l_listing()

        Custom listing with explicit columns::

            from fleet.tlg import Column

            from fleet.tlg.lb_namespace import LBListingSpec

            spec = LBListingSpec(
                columns=[
                    Column(field="USUBJID", label="Subject"),
                    Column(field="PARAM", label="Parameter"),
                    Column(field="AVAL", label="Result"),
                ],
                sort_by=["USUBJID"],
            )
            listing = adlb.tlg.lb.l_listing(spec=spec)
    """
    spec = spec or LBListingSpec()
    spec.validate_dataframe(self._df)

    df = self._df
    dataset_filter = resolve_filter(spec.dataset_filter)
    if dataset_filter is not None:
        df = df.filter(dataset_filter)
    elif "ANRIND" in df.columns:
        # Default: abnormalities only (exclude normal / missing indicators).
        df = df.filter(
            pl.col("ANRIND").is_not_null()
            & (~pl.col("ANRIND").str.to_uppercase().is_in(["NORMAL", "N", ""]))
        )

    # Select only requested columns (that exist)
    available = set(df.columns)
    select_cols = [c.field for c in spec.columns if c.field in available]
    df = df.select(select_cols)

    # Rename to labels
    rename_map = {c.field: c.label for c in spec.columns if c.label and c.field in available}
    if rename_map:
        df = df.rename(rename_map)

    # Sort
    sort_cols = []
    for s in spec.sort_by:
        col_name = rename_map.get(s, s)
        if col_name in df.columns:
            sort_cols.append(col_name)
    if sort_cols:
        df = df.sort(sort_cols)

    return df

    def check(
    self,
    *,
    spec: LBSummarySpec | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Run pre-validation diagnostics without computing.

    Args:
        spec: Optional spec to check against.  If ``None``, the
            default ``LBSummarySpec`` is used.

    Returns:
        list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if all checks pass).

    Examples:
        Check data readiness::

            report = adlb.tlg.lb.check()
    """
    spec = spec or LBSummarySpec()
    diagnostics = spec.check(self._df)

    available = set(self._df.columns)
    for row_def in spec.rows:
        if row_def.field not in available:
            diagnostics.append(
                f"WARNING: Column '{row_def.field}' not present — "
                f"'{row_def.label or row_def.field}' sub-analysis will be skipped."
            )

    return diagnostics

    class MHTLGNamespace(BuilderVerbsMixin):
    """Medical-history tables, accessed as ``df.tlg.mh``."""

    _builder_context = "t_mh_summary"
    _builder_specs = {"t_summary": MHSummarySpec}

    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        self._df = df

    def t_summary(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: str | None = None,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        spec: MHSummarySpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Produce a medical-history summary ARD (n / % subjects by SOC → PT).

        Args:
            groupby: Treatment-arm column; overrides ``spec.columns[0]``.
            adsl: ADSL for big-N denominators (percentages).
            spec: Optional ``MHSummarySpec`` override.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: {cards}-compatible ARD.

        Examples:
            ``ard = admh.tlg.mh.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)``
        """
        spec = spec or MHSummarySpec()
        group_col = groupby or (spec.columns[0] if spec.columns else "TRTA")
        spec.validate_dataframe(self._df, group_col=group_col)
        return summarize_ard(
            fill_uncoded(self._df, ["MHBODSYS", "MHDECOD"]),
            rows=spec.rows,
            stats=spec.statistics,
            context="t_mh_summary",
            group_col=group_col,
            pools=spec.pools,
            column_order=spec.column_order,
            adsl=adsl,
            adsl_filter=spec.adsl_filter,
            dataset_filter=spec.dataset_filter,
            header_rows=spec.header_rows,
            nested=True,
        )

    def check(self, *, spec: MHSummarySpec | None = None) -> list[str]:
        """Run pre-validation diagnostics without computing."""
        spec = spec or MHSummarySpec()
        diagnostics = spec.check(self._df)
        available = set(self._df.columns)
        for row_def in spec.rows:
            if row_def.field not in available:
                diagnostics.append(f"WARNING: Column '{row_def.field}' not present — skipped.")
        return diagnostics

    @pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("tlg")
class TLGNamespace:
    """Root TLG namespace, accessed as ``df.tlg``.

    This namespace acts as a router to domain-specific sub-namespaces.
    It holds a reference to the underlying DataFrame and passes it to
    sub-namespaces on property access.
    """

    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        self._df = df

    @property
    def ae(self) -> AETLGNamespace:
        """AE (adverse event) tables and listings."""
        from .ae_namespace import AETLGNamespace

        return AETLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def vs(self) -> VSTLGNamespace:
        """Vital-signs summary tables."""
        from .vs_namespace import VSTLGNamespace

        return VSTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def cm(self) -> CMTLGNamespace:
        """Concomitant-medication tables."""
        from .cm_namespace import CMTLGNamespace

        return CMTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def ex(self) -> EXTLGNamespace:
        """Exposure tables."""
        from .ex_namespace import EXTLGNamespace

        return EXTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def dm(self) -> DMTLGNamespace:
        """Demographic tables."""
        from .dm_namespace import DMTLGNamespace

        return DMTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def ds(self) -> DSTLGNamespace:
        """Disposition, deaths, enrollment, and deviation tables."""
        from .ds_namespace import DSTLGNamespace

        return DSTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def eg(self) -> EGTLGNamespace:
        """ECG summary tables."""
        from .eg_namespace import EGTLGNamespace

        return EGTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def lb(self) -> LBTLGNamespace:
        """Laboratory tables and listings."""
        from .lb_namespace import LBTLGNamespace

        return LBTLGNamespace(self._df)

    @property
    def mh(self) -> MHTLGNamespace:
        """Medical-history tables."""
        from .mh_namespace import MHTLGNamespace

        return MHTLGNamespace(self._df)

    def check(self) -> list[str]:
        """Run pre-validation diagnostics across all sub-namespaces.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Diagnostic messages from all sub-namespace specs.
        """
        from .ae_namespace import AETLGNamespace

        diagnostics: list[str] = []
        ae_ns = AETLGNamespace(self._df)
        diagnostics.extend(ae_ns.check())
        return diagnostics

    class VSTLGNamespace(BuilderVerbsMixin):
    """Vital-signs tables and diagnostics.

    Accessed as ``df.tlg.vs``.  Supports both spec-driven
    (``t_summary(spec=...)``) and inline builder (``df.tlg.vs.by(...)``)
    workflows.

    Args:
        df: A Polars DataFrame containing ADaM VS-level data.
    """

    _builder_context = "t_vs_summary"
    _builder_specs = {"t_summary": VSSummarySpec}

    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        self._df = df

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Summary table                                                        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def t_summary(
        self,
        *,
        groupby: str | None = None,
        adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
        spec: VSSummarySpec | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Produce a VS summary ARD (Analysis Results Dataset).

        Computes big-N from *adsl*, then continuous statistics for each
        parameter (or custom row hierarchy).

        Args:
            groupby: Treatment arm column name.  Overrides
                ``spec.columns[0]`` when given.
            adsl: ADSL DataFrame for big-N denominators.
            spec: Optional ``VSSummarySpec`` override.  If ``None``, the
                default spec is used.

        Returns:
            pl.DataFrame: Long-format {cards}-compatible ARD.

        Examples:
            Zero-config VS summary::

                ard = advs.tlg.vs.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)

            Custom spec with pooled arms::

                from fleet.tlg import VSSummarySpec, GroupPool

                spec = VSSummarySpec(
                    pools=[GroupPool(label="Total", arms="*")],
                )
                ard = advs.tlg.vs.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
        """
        spec = spec or VSSummarySpec()
        group_col = groupby or (spec.columns[0] if spec.columns else "TRTA")
        spec.validate_dataframe(self._df, group_col=group_col)
        return summarize_ard(
            self._df,
            rows=spec.rows,
            stats=spec.statistics,
            context="t_vs_summary",
            group_col=group_col,
            pools=spec.pools,
            column_order=spec.column_order,
            adsl=adsl,
            adsl_filter=spec.adsl_filter,
            dataset_filter=spec.dataset_filter,
            header_rows=spec.header_rows,
            nested=True,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Pre-validation diagnostic                                            #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def check(
        self,
        *,
        spec: VSSummarySpec | None = None,
    ) -> list[str]:
        """Run pre-validation diagnostics without computing.

        Args:
            spec: Optional spec to check against.

        Returns:
            list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if all checks pass).

        Examples:
            Check data readiness::

                report = advs.tlg.vs.check()
        """
        spec = spec or VSSummarySpec()
        diagnostics = spec.check(self._df)

        available = set(self._df.columns)
        for row_def in spec.rows:
            if row_def.field not in available:
                diagnostics.append(
                    f"WARNING: Column '{row_def.field}' not present — "
                    f"'{row_def.label or row_def.field}' sub-analysis will be skipped."
                )

        return diagnostics

    def t_summary(
    self,
    *,
    groupby: str | None = None,
    adsl: pl.DataFrame | None = None,
    spec: VSSummarySpec | None = None,
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Produce a VS summary ARD (Analysis Results Dataset).

    Computes big-N from *adsl*, then continuous statistics for each
    parameter (or custom row hierarchy).

    Args:
        groupby: Treatment arm column name.  Overrides
            ``spec.columns[0]`` when given.
        adsl: ADSL DataFrame for big-N denominators.
        spec: Optional ``VSSummarySpec`` override.  If ``None``, the
            default spec is used.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: Long-format {cards}-compatible ARD.

    Examples:
        Zero-config VS summary::

            ard = advs.tlg.vs.t_summary(groupby="TRTA", adsl=adsl)

        Custom spec with pooled arms::

            from fleet.tlg import VSSummarySpec, GroupPool

            spec = VSSummarySpec(
                pools=[GroupPool(label="Total", arms="*")],
            )
            ard = advs.tlg.vs.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)
    """
    spec = spec or VSSummarySpec()
    group_col = groupby or (spec.columns[0] if spec.columns else "TRTA")
    spec.validate_dataframe(self._df, group_col=group_col)
    return summarize_ard(
        self._df,
        rows=spec.rows,
        stats=spec.statistics,
        context="t_vs_summary",
        group_col=group_col,
        pools=spec.pools,
        column_order=spec.column_order,
        adsl=adsl,
        adsl_filter=spec.adsl_filter,
        dataset_filter=spec.dataset_filter,
        header_rows=spec.header_rows,
        nested=True,
    )

    def check(
    self,
    *,
    spec: VSSummarySpec | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Run pre-validation diagnostics without computing.

    Args:
        spec: Optional spec to check against.

    Returns:
        list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if all checks pass).

    Examples:
        Check data readiness::

            report = advs.tlg.vs.check()
    """
    spec = spec or VSSummarySpec()
    diagnostics = spec.check(self._df)

    available = set(self._df.columns)
    for row_def in spec.rows:
        if row_def.field not in available:
            diagnostics.append(
                f"WARNING: Column '{row_def.field}' not present — "
                f"'{row_def.label or row_def.field}' sub-analysis will be skipped."
            )

    return diagnostics

    def apply_fmt_fn(value: float | None, fmt: str) -> str:
    """Apply a format specifier to a numeric value.

    Supported format patterns:
      - ``"xx"``       → integer (e.g. ``"86"``)
      - ``"xx.x"``     → 1 decimal (e.g. ``"75.2"``)
      - ``"xx.xx"``    → 2 decimals (e.g. ``"8.59"``)
      - ``"xx.xxx"``   → 3 decimals
      - ``"xx.x%"``    → 1 decimal with % suffix

    Args:
        value: The numeric value to format (None → ``""``).
        fmt: The format specifier string.

    Returns:
        str: The formatted string.
    """
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and math.isnan(value)):
        return ""

    # Count decimal places from the "xx.xxx" pattern
    pct_suffix = fmt.endswith("%")
    clean = fmt.rstrip("%")

    if "." in clean:
        decimals = len(clean.split(".")[1])
    else:
        decimals = 0

    formatted = f"{value:.{decimals}f}"
    if pct_suffix:
        formatted += "%"
    return formatted

    def format_ard(ard: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Apply ``fmt_fn`` to every row and produce a ``stat_fmt`` column.

    This mirrors ``{cards}::apply_fmt_fn()`` — takes the ARD and produces
    human-readable formatted strings from the numeric ``stat`` column.

    Args:
        ard: An ARD DataFrame with ``stat`` and ``fmt_fn`` columns.

    Returns:
        pl.DataFrame: The ARD with ``stat_fmt`` column populated.
    """
    if "fmt_fn" not in ard.columns or "stat" not in ard.columns:
        return ard

    formatted = []
    stat_vals = ard["stat"].to_list()
    fmt_vals = ard["fmt_fn"].to_list()

    for val, fmt in zip(stat_vals, fmt_vals):
        if fmt is None:
            formatted.append("" if val is None else str(val))
        else:
            formatted.append(apply_fmt_fn(val, fmt))

    return ard.with_columns(pl.Series("stat_fmt", formatted, dtype=pl.Utf8))

    def validate_ard(df: pl.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
    """Validate that *df* conforms to the {cards}-compatible ARD schema.

    Checks required column presence, data types, and structural integrity.
    Group columns (``group1``, ``group2``, etc.) are optional — matching
    {cards} where not all ARDs have grouping.

    Args:
        df: A DataFrame to validate as ARD.

    Returns:
        list[str]: Diagnostic messages (empty if valid).

    Examples:
        Validate an ARD after computation::

            from fleet.tlg._ard import validate_ard

            issues = validate_ard(ard)
            assert issues == [], issues
    """
    issues: list[str] = []

    # Required columns must be present
    missing_required = [c for c in ARD_REQUIRED_COLUMNS if c not in df.columns]
    if missing_required:
        issues.append(f"Missing required ARD columns: {missing_required}")

    # Check for completely unknown columns
    known = set(ARD_SCHEMA.keys())
    extra = [c for c in df.columns if c not in known]
    if extra:
        issues.append(f"Unexpected columns (not in ARD schema): {extra}")

    # Data types (only check columns that exist)
    for col, expected_dtype in ARD_SCHEMA.items():
        if col in df.columns:
            actual = df[col].dtype
            if actual != expected_dtype:
                issues.append(f"Column '{col}': expected {expected_dtype}, got {actual}")

    # Non-empty check
    if len(df) == 0:
        issues.append("ARD is empty (0 rows)")

    return issues

    def resolve_filter(value: Any) -> pl.Expr | None:
    """Resolve a spec filter field to a Polars expression.

    Filters may be given as a ``pl.Expr`` (inline use) or as a string
    expression such as ``'pl.col("SAFFL") == "Y"'`` — the string form is
    the YAML-serializable one, parsed through the same AST-whitelisted
    ``parse_expression`` used by the SDTM/ADaM YAML specs.

    Args:
        value: ``None``, a ``pl.Expr``, or an expression string.

    Returns:
        pl.Expr | None: The resolved expression.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a string expression cannot be parsed.
        TypeError: If the value is neither ``None``, ``str`` nor ``pl.Expr``.
    """
    if value is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, pl.Expr):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return parse_expression(value)
    raise TypeError(
        f"Filter must be a pl.Expr or an expression string, got {type(value).__name__!r}"
    )

    def ard_to_table_model(
    ard: pl.DataFrame,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
) -> TableModel:
    """Shape a long-format ARD into a display-ready ``TableModel``.

    This is the core Phase 2 shaping function.  It:
    1. Extracts big-N from ``stat_name == "N"`` rows → column headers.
    2. Identifies header rows (``variable == ""``) → ``TableRow(row_type="header")``.
    3. Identifies hierarchy rows → ``"group"`` or ``"data"`` row types.
    4. Merges ``n`` + ``pct`` stats into single display cells.

    Args:
        ard: A {cards}-compatible ARD DataFrame.
        metadata: Optional render metadata.  If ``None``, a blank
            ``RenderMetadata`` is used.

    Returns:
        TableModel: A display-ready table model suitable for any renderer.
    """
    meta = metadata or RenderMetadata()

    # ── 1. Extract column order (arms) ──
    # Respect the order already present in the ARD (set by column_order in spec)
    arm_order: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for val in ard["group1_level"].to_list():
        if val and val not in seen:
            arm_order.append(val)
            seen.add(val)

    # ── 2. Extract big-N for column headers ──
    big_n_rows = ard.filter((pl.col("stat_name") == "N") & (pl.col("variable") == ""))
    big_n_map: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in big_n_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
        arm = row["group1_level"]
        val = row["stat"]
        if arm and val is not None:
            big_n_map[arm] = int(val)

    columns = [ColumnHeader(label=arm, big_n=big_n_map.get(arm)) for arm in arm_order]

    # ── 3. Get non-big-N rows ──
    data_rows = ard.filter(~((pl.col("stat_name") == "N") & (pl.col("variable") == "")))

    # ── 4. Determine row hierarchy structure ──
    # Unique (group2_level, variable, variable_level) triples in order —
    # nested ARDs emit the same child level once per parent, so the
    # parent lineage must be part of the display-row identity or cells
    # from different parents collapse into one row (last-write-wins).
    row_keys: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    row_keys_seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    for row in data_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
        key = (row.get("group2_level") or "", row["variable"], row["variable_level"])
        if key not in row_keys_seen:
            row_keys.append(key)
            row_keys_seen.add(key)

    # Determine which variables are "groups" (have children)
    all_variables = [k[1] for k in row_keys if k[1]]
    unique_variables = list(dict.fromkeys(all_variables))
    # If there are 2+ distinct non-empty variables, the first is group level
    has_hierarchy = len(unique_variables) >= 2

    # ── 5. Build display rows ──
    table_rows: list[TableRow] = []

    for group2_level, variable, variable_level in row_keys:
        # Determine row type
        if variable == "":
            # Header row (OverallStat)
            row_type = "header"
            indent = 0
            bold = False
            label = variable_level
        elif has_hierarchy and variable == unique_variables[0]:
            # First variable = group level (SOC), show as group stub
            # Only emit group stub once per variable_level
            row_type = "group"
            indent = 0
            bold = True
            label = variable_level
        elif has_hierarchy:
            # Second+ variable = data level (PT), indented
            row_type = "data"
            indent = 1
            bold = False
            label = variable_level
        else:
            # Single variable = flat
            row_type = "flat"
            indent = 0
            bold = False
            label = variable_level

        # ── Collect cell values per arm ──
        cells: dict[str, str] = {}

        # Filter ARD to this (group2_level, variable, variable_level)
        vl_rows = data_rows.filter(
            (pl.col("group2_level").fill_null("") == group2_level)
            & (pl.col("variable") == variable)
            & (pl.col("variable_level") == variable_level)
        )

        for arm in arm_order:
            arm_rows = vl_rows.filter(pl.col("group1_level") == arm)
            if arm_rows.is_empty():
                cells[arm] = ""
                continue

            # Collect stats for this cell
            stats: dict[str, str] = {}
            for sr in arm_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
                sname = sr["stat_name"]
                # Prefer stat_fmt, fall back to stat
                sfmt = sr.get("stat_fmt") or ""
                if not sfmt and sr["stat"] is not None:
                    sfmt = (
                        str(int(sr["stat"])) if sr["stat"] == int(sr["stat"]) else str(sr["stat"])
                    )
                stats[sname] = sfmt

            # Merge n + pct into single display string
            if "n" in stats and "pct" in stats:
                cells[arm] = _merge_n_pct(stats["n"], stats["pct"])
            elif "n" in stats:
                cells[arm] = stats["n"]
            elif "pct" in stats:
                cells[arm] = stats["pct"]
            elif "mean" in stats:
                # Continuous stats — show each on its own row
                # This path is for when we iterate per stat
                cells[arm] = stats.get("mean", "")
            else:
                # Single stat (n_events, or other)
                val = next(iter(stats.values()), "")
                cells[arm] = val

        # For group stubs in a hierarchy, don't show cells (empty row)
        if row_type == "group":
            cells = {arm: "" for arm in arm_order}

        table_rows.append(
            TableRow(
                label=label,
                row_type=row_type,
                indent=indent,
                cells=cells,
                bold=bold,
            )
        )

    return TableModel(metadata=meta, columns=columns, rows=table_rows)

    def listing_to_model(
    listing: pl.DataFrame,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
) -> ListingModel:
    """Shape a listing DataFrame into a display-ready ``ListingModel``.

    Args:
        listing: A Polars DataFrame from ``l_listing()``.
        metadata: Optional render metadata.

    Returns:
        ListingModel: A display-ready listing model.
    """
    meta = metadata or RenderMetadata()
    col_labels = list(listing.columns)

    data: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for row in listing.iter_rows(named=True):
        data.append({col: str(v) if v is not None else "" for col, v in row.items()})

    return ListingModel(metadata=meta, column_labels=col_labels, data=data)

    def render_html(
    model: TableModel,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style HTML table.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template string.  If given, the
            generated ``<table>`` block replaces the ``{table}`` placeholder,
            enabling embedding in sponsor portals, Quarto documents, or
            interactive dashboards.

    Returns:
        str: Complete HTML string (with ``<style>`` block) or injected
            into *html_wrapper*.
    """
    parts: list[str] = []

    # ── Title / subtitle ──
    has_title = bool(model.metadata.title)
    has_subtitle = bool(model.metadata.subtitle)

    parts.append('<div class="fleet-table-container">')
    parts.append(_SUMMARY_CSS)

    if has_title:
        parts.append(f'<div class="fleet-table-title">{_esc(model.metadata.title)}</div>')
    if has_subtitle:
        parts.append(f'<div class="fleet-table-subtitle">{_esc(model.metadata.subtitle)}</div>')

    # ── Table header ──
    parts.append('<table class="fleet-summary">')
    parts.append("<thead>")
    parts.append("<tr>")
    parts.append(f'<th class="stub-header">{_esc(model.stub_label)}</th>')
    for col in model.columns:
        parts.append(f"<th>{_esc(col.display)}</th>")
    parts.append("</tr>")
    parts.append("</thead>")

    # ── Table body ──
    parts.append("<tbody>")

    # Track whether we've seen hierarchy rows to insert separator
    seen_header = False
    separator_inserted = False

    for row in model.rows:
        # Insert separator between header rows and hierarchy rows
        if row.row_type in ("group", "data", "flat") and seen_header and not separator_inserted:
            parts.append('<tr class="separator-row">')
            parts.append(f'<td colspan="{1 + len(model.columns)}"></td>')
            parts.append("</tr>")
            separator_inserted = True

        if row.row_type == "header":
            seen_header = True

        css_class = f"{row.row_type}-row"
        parts.append(f'<tr class="{css_class}">')

        # Stub cell
        label = _esc(row.label)
        parts.append(f'<td class="stub">{label}</td>')

        # Stat cells
        for col in model.columns:
            val = _esc(row.cells.get(col.label, ""))
            parts.append(f'<td class="stat-cell">{val}</td>')

        parts.append("</tr>")

    parts.append("</tbody>")
    parts.append("</table>")

    # ── Footnotes ──
    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        parts.append('<div class="fleet-table-footnotes">')
        for fn in model.metadata.footnotes:
            parts.append(f"<p>{_esc(fn)}</p>")
        parts.append("</div>")

    parts.append("</div>")

    html = "\n".join(parts)

    if html_wrapper is not None:
        return html_wrapper.replace("{table}", html)

    return html

    def render_listing_html(
    model: ListingModel,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` as a pharma-style HTML listing.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template string with ``{table}``
            placeholder.

    Returns:
        str: Complete HTML string (with ``<style>`` block).
    """
    parts: list[str] = []

    parts.append('<div class="fleet-listing-container">')
    parts.append(_LISTING_CSS)

    if model.metadata.title:
        parts.append(f'<div class="fleet-listing-title">{_esc(model.metadata.title)}</div>')
    if model.metadata.subtitle:
        parts.append(f'<div class="fleet-listing-subtitle">{_esc(model.metadata.subtitle)}</div>')

    parts.append('<table class="fleet-listing">')

    # ── Header ──
    parts.append("<thead>")
    parts.append("<tr>")
    for label in model.column_labels:
        parts.append(f"<th>{_esc(label)}</th>")
    parts.append("</tr>")
    parts.append("</thead>")

    # ── Body ──
    parts.append("<tbody>")
    for row_data in model.data:
        parts.append("<tr>")
        for label in model.column_labels:
            val = _esc(row_data.get(label, ""))
            parts.append(f"<td>{val}</td>")
        parts.append("</tr>")
    parts.append("</tbody>")

    parts.append("</table>")

    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        parts.append('<div class="fleet-listing-footnotes">')
        for fn in model.metadata.footnotes:
            parts.append(f"<p>{_esc(fn)}</p>")
        parts.append("</div>")

    parts.append("</div>")

    html = "\n".join(parts)

    if html_wrapper is not None:
        return html_wrapper.replace("{table}", html)

    return html

    def render_listing_pdf(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` to a PDF file via WeasyPrint.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model.
        path: Output PDF file path.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}`` placeholder.

    Returns:
        Path: The written PDF path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If WeasyPrint is not installed.
    """
    try:
        import weasyprint  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "WeasyPrint is required for PDF export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add weasyprint\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pdf]"
        ) from None

    html = render_listing_html(model, html_wrapper=html_wrapper)
    doc = (
        "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
        '<html><head><meta charset="utf-8">'
        "<style>"
        "@page { size: landscape; margin: 1cm; }"
        "body { font-family: 'Courier New', Courier, monospace; font-size: 9pt; }"
        "</style></head><body>\n"
        f"{html}\n"
        "</body></html>"
    )
    p = Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    weasyprint.HTML(string=doc).write_pdf(str(p))
    return p

    def render_listing_pptx(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a flat data listing as an editable PowerPoint
    table.  The listing can be modified after export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE listing to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import listing_to_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_listing_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7.1", subtitle="AE Listing")
            model = listing_to_model(listing_df, meta)
            render_listing_pptx(model, "ae_listing.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)

    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    # ── Title + subtitle ──
    top = Inches(0.3)
    if model.metadata.title:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.title
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.45)

    if model.metadata.subtitle:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.subtitle
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.4)

    top += Inches(0.1)

    # ── Table ──
    n_cols = len(model.column_labels)
    n_rows = 1 + len(model.data)  # header + data

    table_width = Inches(12.3)
    table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
    table_left = Inches(0.5)

    tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height)
    table = tbl_shape.table

    col_width = int(table_width / max(n_cols, 1))
    for ci in range(n_cols):
        table.columns[ci].width = Emu(col_width)

    # Headers
    for ci, lbl in enumerate(model.column_labels):
        cell = table.cell(0, ci)
        cell.text = ""
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = lbl
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
        p.font.bold = True
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_bg"])
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_fg"])

    # Data rows
    for ri, row_data in enumerate(model.data, start=1):
        bg = th["alt_row_bg"] if ri % 2 == 0 else None
        for ci, lbl in enumerate(model.column_labels):
            cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = row_data.get(lbl, "")
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
            if bg:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)

    # ── Footnotes ──
    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
        fn_text = "\n".join(model.metadata.footnotes)
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = fn_text
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

    The output is editable: users can modify fonts, colours, text, and layout in PowerPoint or LibreOffice Impress after export.

    def render_pptx(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a fully editable PowerPoint table with:
    - Title and subtitle from ``RenderMetadata``
    - Column headers with optional (N=xx) display
    - Row hierarchy with indentation and bold formatting
    - Footnotes rendered below the table

    The output is editable: users can modify fonts, colours, text, and
    layout in PowerPoint or LibreOffice Impress after export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.  Keys include
            ``font_name``, ``font_size_body``, ``header_bg``, etc.
            See ``_DEFAULT_THEME`` for all available keys.

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary ARD to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import ard_to_table_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1", subtitle="AE Summary")
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
            render_pptx(model, "ae_summary.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)

    prs = Presentation()
    # Landscape 16:9
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank layout
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    # ── Title + subtitle ──
    top = Inches(0.3)
    if model.metadata.title:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.title
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.45)

    if model.metadata.subtitle:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.subtitle
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.4)

    top += Inches(0.1)

    # ── Table dimensions ──
    n_cols = 1 + len(model.columns)  # stub + arms
    n_rows = 1 + len(model.rows)  # header + data rows

    table_width = Inches(12.3)
    table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
    table_left = Inches(0.5)

    tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height)
    table = tbl_shape.table

    # Distribute column widths: stub gets 30%, rest evenly split
    stub_width = int(table_width * 0.30)
    arm_width = int((table_width - stub_width) / max(len(model.columns), 1))
    table.columns[0].width = Emu(stub_width)
    for ci in range(1, n_cols):
        table.columns[ci].width = Emu(arm_width)

    # ── Helper: set cell text + style ──
    def _set_cell(
        row_idx: int,
        col_idx: int,
        text: str,
        *,
        bold: bool = False,
        font_size: int | None = None,
        bg: str | None = None,
        fg: str | None = None,
        align: Any = PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
        indent: int = 0,
    ) -> None:
        cell = table.cell(row_idx, col_idx)
        cell.text = ""
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = text
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size or th["font_size_body"])
        p.font.bold = bold
        p.alignment = align
        if fg:
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(fg)
        if bg:
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)
        if indent:
            p.level = min(indent, 8)

    # ── Column headers ──
    _set_cell(0, 0, model.stub_label, bold=True, bg=th["header_bg"], fg=th["header_fg"])
    for ci, col in enumerate(model.columns, start=1):
        _set_cell(
            0,
            ci,
            col.display,
            bold=True,
            bg=th["header_bg"],
            fg=th["header_fg"],
            align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
        )

    # ── Data rows ──
    for ri, row in enumerate(model.rows, start=1):
        # Row background
        if row.row_type == "group":
            bg = th["group_bg"]
        elif ri % 2 == 0:
            bg = th["alt_row_bg"]
        else:
            bg = None

        # Stub cell
        indent_spaces = "  " * row.indent
        _set_cell(
            ri,
            0,
            f"{indent_spaces}{row.label}",
            bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
            bg=bg,
        )

        # Value cells
        for ci, col in enumerate(model.columns, start=1):
            val = row.cells.get(col.label, "")
            _set_cell(
                ri,
                ci,
                val,
                bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
                bg=bg,
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
            )

    # ── Footnotes ──
    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
        fn_text = "\n".join(model.metadata.footnotes)
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = fn_text
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

    def ard_to_table_model(
    ard: pl.DataFrame,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
) -> TableModel:
    """Shape a long-format ARD into a display-ready ``TableModel``.

    This is the core Phase 2 shaping function.  It:
    1. Extracts big-N from ``stat_name == "N"`` rows → column headers.
    2. Identifies header rows (``variable == ""``) → ``TableRow(row_type="header")``.
    3. Identifies hierarchy rows → ``"group"`` or ``"data"`` row types.
    4. Merges ``n`` + ``pct`` stats into single display cells.

    Args:
        ard: A {cards}-compatible ARD DataFrame.
        metadata: Optional render metadata.  If ``None``, a blank
            ``RenderMetadata`` is used.

    Returns:
        TableModel: A display-ready table model suitable for any renderer.
    """
    meta = metadata or RenderMetadata()

    # ── 1. Extract column order (arms) ──
    # Respect the order already present in the ARD (set by column_order in spec)
    arm_order: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for val in ard["group1_level"].to_list():
        if val and val not in seen:
            arm_order.append(val)
            seen.add(val)

    # ── 2. Extract big-N for column headers ──
    big_n_rows = ard.filter((pl.col("stat_name") == "N") & (pl.col("variable") == ""))
    big_n_map: dict[str, int] = {}
    for row in big_n_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
        arm = row["group1_level"]
        val = row["stat"]
        if arm and val is not None:
            big_n_map[arm] = int(val)

    columns = [ColumnHeader(label=arm, big_n=big_n_map.get(arm)) for arm in arm_order]

    # ── 3. Get non-big-N rows ──
    data_rows = ard.filter(~((pl.col("stat_name") == "N") & (pl.col("variable") == "")))

    # ── 4. Determine row hierarchy structure ──
    # Unique (group2_level, variable, variable_level) triples in order —
    # nested ARDs emit the same child level once per parent, so the
    # parent lineage must be part of the display-row identity or cells
    # from different parents collapse into one row (last-write-wins).
    row_keys: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    row_keys_seen: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    for row in data_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
        key = (row.get("group2_level") or "", row["variable"], row["variable_level"])
        if key not in row_keys_seen:
            row_keys.append(key)
            row_keys_seen.add(key)

    # Determine which variables are "groups" (have children)
    all_variables = [k[1] for k in row_keys if k[1]]
    unique_variables = list(dict.fromkeys(all_variables))
    # If there are 2+ distinct non-empty variables, the first is group level
    has_hierarchy = len(unique_variables) >= 2

    # ── 5. Build display rows ──
    table_rows: list[TableRow] = []

    for group2_level, variable, variable_level in row_keys:
        # Determine row type
        if variable == "":
            # Header row (OverallStat)
            row_type = "header"
            indent = 0
            bold = False
            label = variable_level
        elif has_hierarchy and variable == unique_variables[0]:
            # First variable = group level (SOC), show as group stub
            # Only emit group stub once per variable_level
            row_type = "group"
            indent = 0
            bold = True
            label = variable_level
        elif has_hierarchy:
            # Second+ variable = data level (PT), indented
            row_type = "data"
            indent = 1
            bold = False
            label = variable_level
        else:
            # Single variable = flat
            row_type = "flat"
            indent = 0
            bold = False
            label = variable_level

        # ── Collect cell values per arm ──
        cells: dict[str, str] = {}

        # Filter ARD to this (group2_level, variable, variable_level)
        vl_rows = data_rows.filter(
            (pl.col("group2_level").fill_null("") == group2_level)
            & (pl.col("variable") == variable)
            & (pl.col("variable_level") == variable_level)
        )

        for arm in arm_order:
            arm_rows = vl_rows.filter(pl.col("group1_level") == arm)
            if arm_rows.is_empty():
                cells[arm] = ""
                continue

            # Collect stats for this cell
            stats: dict[str, str] = {}
            for sr in arm_rows.iter_rows(named=True):
                sname = sr["stat_name"]
                # Prefer stat_fmt, fall back to stat
                sfmt = sr.get("stat_fmt") or ""
                if not sfmt and sr["stat"] is not None:
                    sfmt = (
                        str(int(sr["stat"])) if sr["stat"] == int(sr["stat"]) else str(sr["stat"])
                    )
                stats[sname] = sfmt

            # Merge n + pct into single display string
            if "n" in stats and "pct" in stats:
                cells[arm] = _merge_n_pct(stats["n"], stats["pct"])
            elif "n" in stats:
                cells[arm] = stats["n"]
            elif "pct" in stats:
                cells[arm] = stats["pct"]
            elif "mean" in stats:
                # Continuous stats — show each on its own row
                # This path is for when we iterate per stat
                cells[arm] = stats.get("mean", "")
            else:
                # Single stat (n_events, or other)
                val = next(iter(stats.values()), "")
                cells[arm] = val

        # For group stubs in a hierarchy, don't show cells (empty row)
        if row_type == "group":
            cells = {arm: "" for arm in arm_order}

        table_rows.append(
            TableRow(
                label=label,
                row_type=row_type,
                indent=indent,
                cells=cells,
                bold=bold,
            )
        )

    return TableModel(metadata=meta, columns=columns, rows=table_rows)

    def listing_to_model(
    listing: pl.DataFrame,
    metadata: RenderMetadata | None = None,
) -> ListingModel:
    """Shape a listing DataFrame into a display-ready ``ListingModel``.

    Args:
        listing: A Polars DataFrame from ``l_listing()``.
        metadata: Optional render metadata.

    Returns:
        ListingModel: A display-ready listing model.
    """
    meta = metadata or RenderMetadata()
    col_labels = list(listing.columns)

    data: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for row in listing.iter_rows(named=True):
        data.append({col: str(v) if v is not None else "" for col, v in row.items()})

    return ListingModel(metadata=meta, column_labels=col_labels, data=data)

    def render_html(
    model: TableModel,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` as a pharma-style HTML table.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template string.  If given, the
            generated ``<table>`` block replaces the ``{table}`` placeholder,
            enabling embedding in sponsor portals, Quarto documents, or
            interactive dashboards.

    Returns:
        str: Complete HTML string (with ``<style>`` block) or injected
            into *html_wrapper*.
    """
    parts: list[str] = []

    # ── Title / subtitle ──
    has_title = bool(model.metadata.title)
    has_subtitle = bool(model.metadata.subtitle)

    parts.append('<div class="fleet-table-container">')
    parts.append(_SUMMARY_CSS)

    if has_title:
        parts.append(f'<div class="fleet-table-title">{_esc(model.metadata.title)}</div>')
    if has_subtitle:
        parts.append(f'<div class="fleet-table-subtitle">{_esc(model.metadata.subtitle)}</div>')

    # ── Table header ──
    parts.append('<table class="fleet-summary">')
    parts.append("<thead>")
    parts.append("<tr>")
    parts.append(f'<th class="stub-header">{_esc(model.stub_label)}</th>')
    for col in model.columns:
        parts.append(f"<th>{_esc(col.display)}</th>")
    parts.append("</tr>")
    parts.append("</thead>")

    # ── Table body ──
    parts.append("<tbody>")

    # Track whether we've seen hierarchy rows to insert separator
    seen_header = False
    separator_inserted = False

    for row in model.rows:
        # Insert separator between header rows and hierarchy rows
        if row.row_type in ("group", "data", "flat") and seen_header and not separator_inserted:
            parts.append('<tr class="separator-row">')
            parts.append(f'<td colspan="{1 + len(model.columns)}"></td>')
            parts.append("</tr>")
            separator_inserted = True

        if row.row_type == "header":
            seen_header = True

        css_class = f"{row.row_type}-row"
        parts.append(f'<tr class="{css_class}">')

        # Stub cell
        label = _esc(row.label)
        parts.append(f'<td class="stub">{label}</td>')

        # Stat cells
        for col in model.columns:
            val = _esc(row.cells.get(col.label, ""))
            parts.append(f'<td class="stat-cell">{val}</td>')

        parts.append("</tr>")

    parts.append("</tbody>")
    parts.append("</table>")

    # ── Footnotes ──
    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        parts.append('<div class="fleet-table-footnotes">')
        for fn in model.metadata.footnotes:
            parts.append(f"<p>{_esc(fn)}</p>")
        parts.append("</div>")

    parts.append("</div>")

    html = "\n".join(parts)

    if html_wrapper is not None:
        return html_wrapper.replace("{table}", html)

    return html

    def render_listing_html(
    model: ListingModel,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` as a pharma-style HTML listing.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template string with ``{table}``
            placeholder.

    Returns:
        str: Complete HTML string (with ``<style>`` block).
    """
    parts: list[str] = []

    parts.append('<div class="fleet-listing-container">')
    parts.append(_LISTING_CSS)

    if model.metadata.title:
        parts.append(f'<div class="fleet-listing-title">{_esc(model.metadata.title)}</div>')
    if model.metadata.subtitle:
        parts.append(f'<div class="fleet-listing-subtitle">{_esc(model.metadata.subtitle)}</div>')

    parts.append('<table class="fleet-listing">')

    # ── Header ──
    parts.append("<thead>")
    parts.append("<tr>")
    for label in model.column_labels:
        parts.append(f"<th>{_esc(label)}</th>")
    parts.append("</tr>")
    parts.append("</thead>")

    # ── Body ──
    parts.append("<tbody>")
    for row_data in model.data:
        parts.append("<tr>")
        for label in model.column_labels:
            val = _esc(row_data.get(label, ""))
            parts.append(f"<td>{val}</td>")
        parts.append("</tr>")
    parts.append("</tbody>")

    parts.append("</table>")

    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        parts.append('<div class="fleet-listing-footnotes">')
        for fn in model.metadata.footnotes:
            parts.append(f"<p>{_esc(fn)}</p>")
        parts.append("</div>")

    parts.append("</div>")

    html = "\n".join(parts)

    if html_wrapper is not None:
        return html_wrapper.replace("{table}", html)

    return html

    def render_pdf(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    html_wrapper: str | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` to a PDF file via WeasyPrint.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model.
        path: Output PDF file path.
        html_wrapper: Optional HTML template with ``{table}`` placeholder.

    Returns:
        Path: The written PDF path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If WeasyPrint is not installed.
    """
    try:
        import weasyprint  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "WeasyPrint is required for PDF export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add weasyprint\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pdf]"
        ) from None

    html = render_html(model, html_wrapper=html_wrapper)
    # Wrap in a minimal HTML document for WeasyPrint
    doc = (
        "<!DOCTYPE html>\n"
        '<html><head><meta charset="utf-8">'
        "<style>"
        "@page { size: landscape; margin: 1cm; }"
        "body { font-family: 'Courier New', Courier, monospace; font-size: 9pt; }"
        "</style></head><body>\n"
        f"{html}\n"
        "</body></html>"
    )
    p = Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    weasyprint.HTML(string=doc).write_pdf(str(p))
    return p

    def render_pptx(
    model: TableModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``TableModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a fully editable PowerPoint table with:
    - Title and subtitle from ``RenderMetadata``
    - Column headers with optional (N=xx) display
    - Row hierarchy with indentation and bold formatting
    - Footnotes rendered below the table

    The output is editable: users can modify fonts, colours, text, and
    layout in PowerPoint or LibreOffice Impress after export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready table model from ``ard_to_table_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.  Keys include
            ``font_name``, ``font_size_body``, ``header_bg``, etc.
            See ``_DEFAULT_THEME`` for all available keys.

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE summary ARD to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import ard_to_table_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Table 14.3.1.1", subtitle="AE Summary")
            model = ard_to_table_model(ard, meta)
            render_pptx(model, "ae_summary.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)

    prs = Presentation()
    # Landscape 16:9
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank layout
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    # ── Title + subtitle ──
    top = Inches(0.3)
    if model.metadata.title:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.title
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.45)

    if model.metadata.subtitle:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.subtitle
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.4)

    top += Inches(0.1)

    # ── Table dimensions ──
    n_cols = 1 + len(model.columns)  # stub + arms
    n_rows = 1 + len(model.rows)  # header + data rows

    table_width = Inches(12.3)
    table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
    table_left = Inches(0.5)

    tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height)
    table = tbl_shape.table

    # Distribute column widths: stub gets 30%, rest evenly split
    stub_width = int(table_width * 0.30)
    arm_width = int((table_width - stub_width) / max(len(model.columns), 1))
    table.columns[0].width = Emu(stub_width)
    for ci in range(1, n_cols):
        table.columns[ci].width = Emu(arm_width)

    # ── Helper: set cell text + style ──
    def _set_cell(
        row_idx: int,
        col_idx: int,
        text: str,
        *,
        bold: bool = False,
        font_size: int | None = None,
        bg: str | None = None,
        fg: str | None = None,
        align: Any = PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
        indent: int = 0,
    ) -> None:
        cell = table.cell(row_idx, col_idx)
        cell.text = ""
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = text
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size or th["font_size_body"])
        p.font.bold = bold
        p.alignment = align
        if fg:
            p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(fg)
        if bg:
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)
        if indent:
            p.level = min(indent, 8)

    # ── Column headers ──
    _set_cell(0, 0, model.stub_label, bold=True, bg=th["header_bg"], fg=th["header_fg"])
    for ci, col in enumerate(model.columns, start=1):
        _set_cell(
            0,
            ci,
            col.display,
            bold=True,
            bg=th["header_bg"],
            fg=th["header_fg"],
            align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
        )

    # ── Data rows ──
    for ri, row in enumerate(model.rows, start=1):
        # Row background
        if row.row_type == "group":
            bg = th["group_bg"]
        elif ri % 2 == 0:
            bg = th["alt_row_bg"]
        else:
            bg = None

        # Stub cell
        indent_spaces = "  " * row.indent
        _set_cell(
            ri,
            0,
            f"{indent_spaces}{row.label}",
            bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
            bg=bg,
        )

        # Value cells
        for ci, col in enumerate(model.columns, start=1):
            val = row.cells.get(col.label, "")
            _set_cell(
                ri,
                ci,
                val,
                bold=row.bold or row.row_type == "header",
                bg=bg,
                align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER,
            )

    # ── Footnotes ──
    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
        fn_text = "\n".join(model.metadata.footnotes)
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = fn_text
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)

    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    # ── Title + subtitle ──
    top = Inches(0.3)
    if model.metadata.title:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.title
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.45)

    if model.metadata.subtitle:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.subtitle
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.4)

    top += Inches(0.1)

    # ── Table ──
    n_cols = len(model.column_labels)
    n_rows = 1 + len(model.data)  # header + data

    table_width = Inches(12.3)
    table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
    table_left = Inches(0.5)

    tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height)
    table = tbl_shape.table

    col_width = int(table_width / max(n_cols, 1))
    for ci in range(n_cols):
        table.columns[ci].width = Emu(col_width)

    # Headers
    for ci, lbl in enumerate(model.column_labels):
        cell = table.cell(0, ci)
        cell.text = ""
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = lbl
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
        p.font.bold = True
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_bg"])
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_fg"])

    # Data rows
    for ri, row_data in enumerate(model.data, start=1):
        bg = th["alt_row_bg"] if ri % 2 == 0 else None
        for ci, lbl in enumerate(model.column_labels):
            cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = row_data.get(lbl, "")
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
            if bg:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)

    # ── Footnotes ──
    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
        fn_text = "\n".join(model.metadata.footnotes)
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = fn_text
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

    options: show_root_heading: true heading_level: 4
